summary.text:
Let me design the FB logic.

State: Alarm, Acknowledged, prevFault internal.

Per scan:
rise := Fault AND NOT prevFault.

Priority:
1. If rise: Alarm := TRUE; Acknowledged := FALSE.
2. Else if Reset AND NOT Fault: Alarm := FALSE; Acknowledged := FALSE.
3. Else: if Fault then Alarm := TRUE; if Ack AND Alarm(pre-state? qAlarm) ... let's check spec.

Requirements: "A Fault sets Alarm. A rising Fault also clears Acknowledged, taking priority over Ack on that scan. While Fault remains TRUE, Ack can set Acknowledged. When Fault is FALSE the alarm remains latched; Ack can acknowledge that retained alarm. Reset clears both values only when Fault is FALSE, taking priority over Ack then. A new Fault rising edge reannunciates even if an old alarm was already latched."

P6: G((!rise & !Reset & Ack & qAlarm) -> Acknowledged). So Ack only sets Acknowledged when qAlarm (pre-scan alarm) true, and not rise, not Reset. Note Reset blocks Ack even when Fault true? P6 says !Reset required. Hmm. Let's check reset_priority test step 2: Fault=true, Ack=true, Reset=true -> Acknowledged true. So Ack works with Reset when Fault true! But P6 says !Reset... conflict.

Wait test reset_priority step 2: initial after step1: Alarm=true, Ack=false. Step2 Fault true, Ack true, Reset true -> expected Acknowledged true. Reset is true but Fault true so reset doesn't clear. So Ack applies. So P6 formula as stated doesn't hold for that scan. Hmm, maybe P6 qAlarm but Reset condition... The formula in spec may be imperfect, but tests are authoritative. Let's just follow tests/safety priority.

Actually let me re-read P6: G((!rise & !Reset & Ack & qAlarm) -> Acknowledged). This is an implication, not biconditional. It doesn't forbid Acknowledged when Reset true. So it's fine—it's just a one-directional guarantee. So Ack can set Acknowledged in more cases. Good.

Now condition for reset: Reset AND NOT Fault clears both, priority over Ack. Otherwise Ack when qAlarm sets Acknowledged (and Fault sets Alarm).

Let's construct:

rise := Fault AND NOT prevFault;

IF rise THEN
  Alarm := TRUE;
  Acknowledged := FALSE;
ELSIF Reset AND NOT Fault THEN
  Alarm := FALSE;
  Acknowledged := FALSE;
ELSE
  IF Fault THEN Alarm := TRUE; END_IF
  IF Ack AND Alarm THEN Acknowledged := TRUE; END_IF
END_IF
prevFault := Fault;
Horn := Alarm AND NOT Acknowledged;

Check test annunciate:
step0: F0 A0 R0, qAlarm false. rise=false, not reset(F=0 so Reset0). else: Fault false, no. Ack false. Alarm remains false init. good.
step1: F1 A1 R0, prevFault false -> rise true. Alarm=true, Ack=false. Horn=true. good.
step2: F1 A1 R0 prevFault true rise false. else: Fault true->Alarm true. Ack true and Alarm true -> Ack=true. Horn false. good.
step3: F0 A0 R0 rise false, Reset false -> else. Fault false. Ack false. retain Alarm true, Ack true. Horn false. good.
step4: F1 A0 R0 rise true -> Alarm true, Ack false. Horn true. good.
step5: F0 A0 R1: rise false, Reset & !Fault -> clear. good.

reset_priority:
initial reset. step0 F1 A0 R1: rise true (prevFault init false) -> Alarm true Ack false. Horn true. good.
step1 F1 A1 R1: rise false (prev true), Reset&!Fault false -> else. Alarm true, Ack true. good.
step2 F0 A1 R1: rise false, Reset&!Fault true -> clear. good.

All passes. Also considers first invocation: prevFault false init.

Need declaration with VAR_INPUT, VAR_OUTPUT, VAR internal prevFault.

Let me write.

Interface names: Fault, Ack, Reset inputs; Alarm, Acknowledged, Horn outputs.

Declare internal prevFault BOOL.

Let me compile.
